title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned The Workshop Board. Keep it, take The Flat Pattern, choose a challenger, or re-roll.

options.label: The Workshop Board
options.lineage: Delhi NCR enamel trade boards and one-roof workshop rate signs
options.thesis: The whole shop painted on one enamel board: five processes, real capacities, one quote action.
options.viewport: A full-bleed enamel board carries the trade name, the one-roof process chain, calibrated capacity figures, and a red quote plaque.
options.risk: Sign-painter pastiche if the lettering or rules lose precision; long content must extend as further panels, not collapse into a generic page.

raised.raise: The five processes are drawn as one connected load path, not a flat service list.
Capacities are calibrated scales with real thickness limits, not prose claims.
Rate rows use a dense broadside hierarchy with one clear reading order.
A thickness selector updates the cut, shear, and bend limits live.
A material journey strip shows flat sheet to cut to bent to welded with measured states.
One full-bleed enamel ground and one orchestrated scroll transition, with no scattered effects.

options.label: The Flat Pattern
options.lineage: sheet-metal flat patterns and fabrication drawings
options.thesis: The site is the drawing the buyer sends: a flat part that folds into the finished job as you read.
options.viewport: A full-bleed flat pattern with a title block, dimension callouts, and the five processes as bend notes; the folded part lands as you scroll.
options.risk: Blueprint and technical-drawing identities are common in industrial sites; only the folding demonstration and real capacity dimensions keep it from being a skin.

options.label: The Load Path
options.lineage: tensegrity sculpture and engineering force diagrams
options.thesis: The one-roof promise as a tension structure: every process carries and is carried by the next.
options.viewport: A full-height tensegrity column whose cords map cut, bend, shear, weld, and fabricate; selecting a member reveals its capacity and dependency.
options.case: Fuses strongly: the process chain becomes a load path, but lay buyers identify with a workshop board faster.
options.risk: The sculpture can read as an art installation rather than a working fabricator.

options.label: The Capacity Bridge
options.lineage: VU meter bridges and calibrated instrument panels
options.thesis: Every capacity as a calibrated needle: laser, shear, and press brake read against their true limits.
options.viewport: A bridge of capacity meters, each needle set to the confirmed thickness and width limits, with the machine model printed beneath.
options.case: Capacities read instantly, but the audio-desk origin costs audience identification.
options.risk: VU is an audio object; without strict calibration it becomes retro decoration.

options.label: The Trade Broadside
options.thesis: The shop's capabilities printed as one loud, dense trade sheet.
options.viewport: A shouting headline over an engraved image band, with rates and services in two tight columns.
options.risk: The Mexican broadside origin is not the buyer's visual home.
options.kept: Dense two-column rate rows and one unmistakable broadside hierarchy.

options.label: The Cutting List
options.thesis: A live production readout where every job resolves out of falling part codes.
options.viewport: A dark terminal field where job codes fall until one resolution holds a readable drawing.
options.risk: Cyberpunk terminal is a category costume, not the buyer's world.
options.kept: Live, stateful capacity readouts rather than static prose.

options.label: The Heat
options.thesis: Each process as a heat and a blow, with the metal visibly changing state.
options.viewport: A dark forge ground with one white-hot workpiece and force numerals ruled along the blow.
options.risk: Forging is not a confirmed service; the direction would invent capability.
options.kept: A before-and-after material journey with measured states.

options.label: The Molten Field
options.thesis: A single living metal surface with the offer floating on it.
options.viewport: A full-screen shader like cooling metal, with thin tracked labels at the margins and a dissolving route change.
options.risk: Generic immersive spectacle: low product clarity and a real performance cost.
options.kept: One full-bleed committed ground and an orchestrated transition.

canonCard.label: The Category Standard
canonCard.thesis: Dark hero, stat strip, service cards, project gallery, contact CTA.
canonCard.viewport: A dark hero with a headline, three capacity stats, service cards, and a quote button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other fabricator by design.
